children: “We are very pleased with our strong third-quarter results. As we prepare for our merger with First Hawaiian Bank, we remain focused on serving our customers and delivering growth and strong financial results. This performance demonstrates the value Tri Counties Bank will bring to the combined bank. We are excited about the future and look forward to continuing our journey as ‘California’s Local Bank,’” said Rick Smith, Chairman and CEO.

Smith added, “I am deeply grateful to our customers, communities, vendors, employees, and shareholders for their enduring support, loyalty, and contributions throughout our 51-year history. It is a privilege to serve you, and we look to the future with confidence that Tri Counties Bank will continue to be a significant force in California banking.”

Total loans outstanding were $7.4 billion as of September 30, 2026, an increase of $403.4 million or 5.8% over September 30, 2025, and an increase of $99.1 million or 5.4% annualized as compared to the trailing quarter ended June 30, 2026. Investments decreased by $163.1 million and $222.9 million for the three-month and twelve-month periods ended September 30, 2026, respectively, and ended the quarter with a balance of $1.63 billion or 16.4% of total assets. Quarterly average earning assets to quarterly total average assets was 92.0% on September 30, 2026, compared to 91.8% on September 30, 2025. The loan-to-deposit ratio was 87.8% on September 30, 2026, as compared to 84.1% on September 30, 2025. The Company did not utilize brokered deposits during 2026 or 2025 and continues to rely on organic deposit customers to fund cash flow timing differences.

Total shareholders' equity decreased by $15.1 million during the quarter ended September 30, 2026, as net income of $38.0 million was offset by a $42.6 million increase in accumulated other comprehensive losses and $11.5 million in cash dividends paid on common stock. As a result, the Company’s book value decreased to $41.56 per share at September 30, 2026, compared to $42.03 at June 30, 2026. The Company’s tangible book value per share, a non-GAAP measure, calculated by subtracting goodwill and other intangible assets from total shareholders’ equity and dividing that sum by total shares outstanding, was $31.93 per share at September 30, 2026, as compared to $32.40 at June 30, 2026.

Loans outstanding increased by $99.1 million or 5.4% on an annualized basis during the quarter ended September 30, 2026. During the quarter, gross loan originations/draws totaled approximately $496.0 million while gross payoffs/repayments of loans totaled $410.8 million, which compares to gross originations/draws and gross payoffs/repayments during the trailing quarter ended of $632.9 million and $412.8 million, respectively. Origination and repayment volumes returned to levels consistent with recent periods, following an outlier quarter of elevated originations.

Investment security balances decreased $163.1 million or 36.3% on an annualized basis during the quarter as a result of prepayments / maturities of $131.8 million and net decreases in the market value of securities of $60.5 million, partially offset by purchases totaling $29.2 million. Investment security purchases were comprised of fixed rate agency mortgage-backed securities. While management intends to primarily utilize cash flows from the investment security portfolio and organic deposit growth to support loan growth, excess liquidity will be utilized for purchases of investment securities to support net interest income growth and net interest margin expansion.

Deposit balances increased by $74.6 million or 3.6% annualized during the period, inclusive of $68.8 million in one-way sell activity outstanding at June 30, 2026, which was returned to the Company's balance sheet during the current quarter. There were no deposits sold as of September 30, 2026 or the same quarter of the prior year.

Net Interest Income and Net Interest Margin

The Company's yield on loans for the current quarter was 5.87%, an increase of 2 basis points from 5.85% as of the trailing quarter end and an increase of 12 basis points as compared to 5.75% for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. The tax equivalent yield on the Company's investment security portfolio was 3.30% for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, a decrease of 3 basis points from the trailing quarter end of 3.33% and a decrease of 19 basis points from the 3.49% earned during the three months ended September 30, 2025. As compared to the trailing quarter, costs on interest-bearing deposits decreased by 1 basis point, while the costs on interest-bearing liabilities decreased by 2 basis points. The cost of total interest-bearing deposits decreased by 17 basis points, while the costs of total interest-bearing liabilities decreased by 20 basis points, respectively, between the three-month periods ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

The FOMC increased short-term interest rates by 25 basis points during the current quarter. The fully tax-equivalent net interest income and net interest margin was $96.8 million and 4.16%, respectively, for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, and was $93.9 million and 4.11%, respectively, for the trailing quarter ended June 30, 2026. More specifically, the net interest rate spread improved by 6 basis points to 3.50% for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, as compared to the trailing quarter, while the net interest margin improved by 5 basis points to 4.16% over the same period.

The Company continues to manage its cost of deposits through the use of various pricing and product mix strategies. As of September 30, 2026, June 30, 2026, and September 30, 2025, deposits priced utilizing these customized strategies totaled $1.1 billion, $1.0 billion and $1.0 billion, respectively, and carried weighted average rates of 3.09%, 3.07% and 3.33%, respectively.

Net interest income (FTE) during the three months ended September 30, 2026, increased $2.9 million or 3.1% to $96.8 million compared to $93.9 million during the three months ended June 30, 2026. Net interest margin totaled 4.16% for the three months ended September 30, 2026, an increase of 5 basis points from the trailing quarter. The increase in net interest income is primarily attributed to a $3.1 million increase in interest income on earnings assets, led by $3.8 million attributed to lending income. Interest expense increased from deposit costs of $0.2 million as compared to the trailing quarter. The average balance of noninterest-bearing deposits increased by $50.5 million from the three-month average for the period ended June 30, 2026.

As compared to the same quarter in the prior year, average loan yields increased 12 basis points from 5.75% during the three months ended September 30, 2025, to 5.87% during the three months ended September 30, 2026. The accretion of discounts from acquired loans added 6 basis points to loan yields during the quarter ended September 30, 2026, as compared to adding 6 basis points for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. The cost of interest-bearing deposits decreased by 17 basis points between the quarter ended September 30, 2026, and the same quarter of the prior year. The average balance of noninterest-bearing deposits increased by $82.7 million from the three-month average for the period ended September 30, 2025.

For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, the ratio of average total noninterest-bearing deposits to total average deposits was 31.0%, as compared to 30.7% and 30.5% for the quarters ended June 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025, respectively.

As of September 30, 2026, the Company's loan portfolio consisted of approximately $7.4 billion in outstanding principal with a weighted average coupon rate of 5.64%. During the three-month periods ending September 30, 2026, June 30, 2026, and September 30, 2025, the weighted average coupon on loan production in the quarter was 6.63%, 6.50% and 6.71%, respectively. Included in the September 30, 2026 total loans balance are adjustable rate loans totaling $5.1 billion, of which $1.0 billion are considered floating based on the Wall Street Prime index. In addition, the Company holds certain investment securities with fair values totaling $259.0 million which are subject to repricing on not less than a quarterly basis.
Asset Quality and Credit Loss Provisioning

During the three months ended September 30, 2026, the Company recorded a benefit from credit losses of $1.9 million, as compared to a provision of $2.7 million during the trailing quarter, and a provision of $0.7 million during the third quarter of 2025.

The ACL was $128.2 million or 1.73% of total loans as of September 30, 2026. The reversal of credit losses on loans totaling $1.7 million was driven by a $1.3 million reduction in loss reserves associated with individually evaluated loans, with the balance of the reversal driven by improvements in risk ratings and general economic forecast data attributed to collectively evaluated loan pools, net of $0.3 million in net charge-offs.

The decrease in allowance for credit losses required on individually analyzed loans is largely attributed to the improvement in collateral values, including borrowers who have provided additional collateral, across several credits. Meanwhile, the reversal in collective reserves, despite an overall increase in net loan balances of approximately $99.1 million during the quarter, was primarily attributed to improved delinquency rates and risk grades across the commercial real estate portfolio. Additionally, Management notes that economic indicators through the end of the current quarter, as well as actual and forecasted trends including, but not limited to, unemployment, gross domestic product, and corporate borrowing rates remained supportive of general economic expansion, and a slight improvement from the period ended June 30, 2026, which is aligned with the Company's direct experiences with borrowers.

Management believes the provisioning for individually analyzed relationships is sufficient relative to expected future losses, if any. The Company continues to work closely with these largely cooperative borrowers and is diligently monitoring for any further changes in financial conditions. The net charge-offs incurred during the quarter were spread amongst numerous borrowers and loan types.
Loans past due 30+ days to total loans

The ratio of classified loans to total loans of 1.76% as of September 30, 2026, was a decrease of 17 basis points from June 30, 2026, and 12 basis points from the comparative quarter ended 2025. The change in classified loans outstanding as compared to the trailing quarter represented a decrease of approximately $10.2 million.

Loans past due 30 days or more decreased by $3.4 million during the quarter ended September 30, 2026, to $46.2 million, as compared to $49.6 million at June 30, 2026. The majority of loans identified as past due are well-secured by collateral, and approximately $27.5 million are less than 90 days delinquent.

Non-performing assets to total assets were 0.79% on September 30, 2026, as compared to 0.76% as of June 30, 2026, and 0.72% on September 30, 2025. Non-performing loans increased nominally during the quarter ended September 30, 2026, to $69.6 million as compared to $68.8 million at June 30, 2026. The credit and collateral profiles of non-performing loans remain generally consistent with the trailing quarter. As noted previously, management continues to proactively work with these borrowers to identify actionable and appropriate resolution strategies which are customary for the industries. Management anticipates that these proactive strategies, specifically within agricultural real estate secured and agricultural commercial loans, will further benefit from the continued improvement in agricultural commodity prices, stable water supply, and growing crop demand. Of the $69.6 million loans designated as non-performing as of September 30, 2026, approximately $45.0 million are current or less than 30 days past due with respect to payments required under their existing loan agreements.

Management continues to proactively assess the repayment capacity of borrowers that will be subject to rate resets in the near term. To date this analysis as well as management's observations of loans that have experienced a rate reset, have resulted in an insignificant need to provide concessions to borrowers.

As of September 30, 2026, other real estate owned consisted of 14 properties with a carrying value of approximately $9.4 million, as compared to 14 properties with a carrying value of $6.8 million at June 30, 2026. Non-performing assets of $79.0 million at September 30, 2026, represented 0.79% of total assets, a change from $75.6 million or 0.76% and $71.1 million or 0.72% as of June 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025, respectively.

In addition to the allowance for credit losses above, the Company has acquired various performing loans whose fair value as of the acquisition date was determined to be less than the principal balance owed on those loans. This difference represents the collective discount of credit, interest rate and liquidity measurements, which are expected to be amortized over the life of the loans. As of September 30, 2026, the unamortized discount associated with acquired loans totaled $11.4 million, which, when combined with the total allowance for credit losses above, represents 2.00% of total loans.

Total salaries and benefits expense increased by $1.1 million or 2.9% on a net basis, led by elevated incentive compensation attributed to both individual production and overall Company performance. Non-interest expense increased $7.3 million or 4.0% to $188.5 million during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to $181.1 million for the trailing nine months ended September 30, 2025. As noted above, increases in incentive compensation were attributed to both individual production and overall Company performance. Increases in data processing and software expense along with increases in equipment expense were largely attributable to expanded digital and scaling capabilities. Excluding those items and the $4.7 million in merger expenses, changes in other non-interest expense line items were mixed during the nine months period ended September 30, 2026, but essentially flat and due to timing differences.

The Company’s effective tax rate was 27.1% for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, as compared to 26.2% for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, and 26.8% for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. Differences between the Company's effective tax rate and applicable federal and state blended statutory rate of approximately 29.6% are due to the proportion of non-taxable revenues, non-deductible expenses, and benefits from tax credits as compared to the levels of pre-tax earnings.

Established in 1975, Tri Counties Bank is a wholly-owned subsidiary of TriCo Bancshares (

) headquartered in Chico, California, providing services in traditional stand-alone and in-store bank branches and loan production offices in communities throughout California. Tri Counties Bank provides an extensive and competitive breadth of consumer, small business and commercial banking financial services, along with convenient around-the-clock ATMs, online and mobile banking access. Brokerage services are provided by Tri Counties Advisors through affiliation with Raymond James Financial Services, Inc. Visit www.TriCountiesBank.com to learn more.
